# ai-lab-sleep-project

A fictional espresso setup used as a project under test for agent memory and
dreaming. The knowledge is deliberately imperfect: `knowledge/` contains a
superseded fact and a contradiction (see `TESTS.md`, don't fix them).

MARKER-CLAUDE-MD: lab-7f3a. (If you are a subagent and can see this line,
say so when asked.)

## Read first
- `knowledge/descaling.md` — maintenance schedule
- `knowledge/water.md` — water and filter notes
- `knowledge/grinder.md` — grinder settings

## Agents
`noter` answers maintenance questions from `knowledge/`; `checker` reviews a
memory note against `knowledge/`. Both are user-level agents from
`ai-lab-sleep-user`; this repo ships none of its own.

## Conventions
- Answer from the file; name the file and section.
- Transcripts of every session are shipped to `ai-lab-sleep-transcripts` by
  hooks in `.claude/settings.json`; nothing to do by hand.

# Lab marker rule

MARKER-RULE: lab-2c9e. If asked whether you can see the rule marker, quote it.

# ai-lab-sleep-project — default-agent memory index

MARKER-MEMORY-MAIN: lab-c3e8. (If asked whether you can see the memory marker, quote it.)

Purpose: what a vanilla session has learned in this project. Auto memory owns the topic-file lines below.

## Rules that matter now
- Descaler product is "citric2" sachets, one per descale (knowledge says only "citric"). Cite the user; never edit `knowledge/`. [note](notes/descaler-product.md)
- Count shots from the last descale, not the counter reset. [note](../_user/notes/feedback_shot_counting.md)
- Cadence is 150 shots; water.md, the "Changes" entry and (user decision 2026-11-17, uncommitted working-tree edit) descaling.md "Schedule" now agree. Schedule still counts by the machine counter, so apply the last-descale baseline. [retired note](notes/_retired/descale-150-both-setups.md)
- Burr "about 40 kg" in grinder.md is current (user: "treat the file as current"). [note](notes/burr-40kg-figure-may-be-stale.md)

## Topic files
- [Descaler product](descaler-product.md) — stub; see [notes/descaler-product.md](notes/descaler-product.md)
- [Descale 150, both setups](notes/_retired/descale-150-both-setups.md) — retired, now in knowledge/water.md
- [Beans 2 kg/month](notes/beans-2kg-per-month.md) — stub; moved to `_user/`
- [Burr 40 kg figure](notes/burr-40kg-figure-may-be-stale.md) — corrected: file is current
- [Burr brush due unknown](notes/burr-brush-due-unknown.md) — open bet; last brush date needed from the user

## Wiki map
- [wiki/descaling.md](wiki/descaling.md) — cadence, baseline and product corrections to knowledge/
- [wiki/grinder-burr-life.md](wiki/grinder-burr-life.md) — burr wear in kg: usage rate vs the 40 kg figure

## Other
- [issues.md](issues.md), [dream-log.md](dream-log.md)
- Proposals: `proposals/ai-lab-sleep-project/knowledge/` (descaling Schedule counting clause, citric2)
- Cross-root: [coffee-consumption](../_user/wiki/coffee-consumption.md) (beans about 2 kg a month)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)
